title: Insight Builder
description: Keeps the views people read in order: creates and arranges dashboards, refreshes their tiles through each tile's own agent, keeps canvases tidy, and explains what the data products on a knowledge graph can answer — down to the SQL a request would run. What a tile shows and asks, a canvas's content, and running data stay with their own components.

examples.ask: Make a dashboard called Weekly Sales.
examples.outcome: It submits an empty dashboard for your approval; its tiles come from conversations, pinned with the dashboard component.

examples.ask: Refresh the revenue tile on Weekly Sales.
examples.outcome: It finds the tile and submits a refresh: the tile's own agent answers its question again, under its own authority, and the tile shows the new answer.

examples.ask: Which data products can I ask about on the Sales graph?
examples.outcome: It reads the graph's catalog: each product with what it measures, its trust state and whether a validation backs it.

examples.ask: What SQL would revenue by region for last quarter run on the Sales product?
examples.outcome: It compiles the request and shows the SQL — nothing runs. A request the product cannot answer comes back with the closest valid names.

not_offered.what: Adding a tile, or changing what a tile shows or which question it asks
not_offered.why: A tile's content renders in your dashboard, so it is written only by pinning a conversation's own visual; a tile's question decides what another agent is asked on every refresh — both are yours.

not_offered.what: Choosing which agent answers when a tile refreshes
not_offered.why: A tile is always refreshed by its own agent, under that agent's authority.

not_offered.what: How often a dashboard refreshes on its own
not_offered.why: It re-runs every tile's agent on a timer — standing work and spend, like a schedule, so it is yours.
Content is written with the canvas component (TDA_Canvas), under the agent's own enablement — one way in.

not_offered.what: Running a data product query, or running SQL from a canvas
not_offered.why: Reading data is the agent's own access (TDA_DataProduct and its tools), held to its data surface and the deployment's policy; through the platform it would run as you and skip both.

not_offered.what: Creating, validating, deleting or signing a data product
not_offered.why: Defining what a product may answer is modelling, and signing it is yours.
They carry credentials — yours to enter.
